issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and the text before Lemma strangcireiglimitlm say that c(T_n) is diagonalized by F_{p,n}, unlike general quaternion circulants. The lemma proves only that the 2n-by-2n complex representation M(c(T_n)) is unitarily similar, via diag(F,F), to a matrix of 2-by-2 blocks. That argument works for every quaternion circulant, because phi_1 and phi_2 of any circulant are Q_(0,1) circulants. Write c(T_n)=C_1+C_2 q. Then F c(T_n) F^* = Lambda_1 + Lambda_2 J q with J the index-flip permutation. This is X-shaped and not diagonal whenever phi_2(T_n) is nonzero, as in Example ar1 with beta_2 or beta_3 nonzero.

issues.failure_explanation: G[f] is defined with (1,2) entry -phi_2(f) and (2,1) entry conj(phi_2(f)). It is therefore not Hermitian unless phi_2(f)=0, and its eigenvalues are not check f and hat f. The proof's own computation of terms 2 and 3, which uses the oddness of phi_2(f), yields the matrix with +phi_2(f). The last equality equating this to G[f] is false, so the quadratic-form identity (i) is false as stated. The same wrong sign is reused in Lemma strangcireiglimitlm, which claims c(-phi_2(T_n)) has eigenvalues -phi_2(f_m) and that H_s is Hermitian. It is also reused in Appendix A's identification lambda_1(G[f]) = check f.

failure_location.quote: It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define G[f] with (1,2) entry +phi_2(f)(x). Correct the matching sign in the eigenvalue claims in the proof of Lemma strangcireiglimitlm.
issues.overall_effect: Statement (i), the Hermitian claim, and the use of sigma(G[f_m]) in Lemma strangcireiglimitlm are incorrect as written. The formulas for check f and hat f, and all bounds built from them, are those of the corrected matrix.
issues.title: Symbol matrix G[f] has wrong sign and is not Hermitian

diagnostic_evidence.quote: meets Definition \ref{quatgfuncdef} as a generating function for $T_n$

issues.failure_explanation: For s' >= s, put d = s'-s >= 0. The entry is E(x(u-d) conj(x(u))) = conj(E(x(u) conj(x(u-d)))) = conj(eta(d)), not eta(d). So the actual coefficient matrix of (linearsys) is the conjugate (transpose) of the T_n the paper builds. The function in (genf) generates the paper's T_n, not the normal-equation matrix. The numerical matrix tilde H inherits the same orientation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set [T_n]_{s',s} = conj(eta(s'-s)) for s' >= s, and use generating function eta(0)+sum conj(eta(s))exp(psx)+eta(s)exp(-psx). Note that check f is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The link between the prediction normal equations and the generating function (genf) is misstated. The examples' check f and the HPD conclusions are unchanged, because swapping eta and conj(eta) maps phi_1(f)(x) to phi_1(f)(-x) and phi_2 to -phi_2.
issues.title: Covariance matrix entries placed in the wrong triangle
issues.why_classification: This is a local orientation correction. All theoretical conclusions for the application survive.

issues.failure_explanation: For even n, Strang's first column keeps only t_k with |k| <= n/2-1 and puts 0 in position n/2. The circulant eigenvalues are therefore values of the partial sum f_{n/2-1}, not f_{floor(n/2)}. The term of order n/2, evaluated at x = 2 pi s/n, contributes (-1)^s times a generally nonzero quantity. So the exact spectral identity in (i) is false for every even n, including all tested n = 2^k.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace m = floor(n/2) by floor((n-1)/2) in the partial-sum index, keeping the union over s = 0,...,floor(n/2).
issues.overall_effect: Part (i) is incorrect for even n. Part (ii) and the downstream clustering and convergence results are unaffected, since both partial sums converge uniformly to f.
issues.title: Wrong partial-sum order in Strang eigenvalue formula for even n
issues.why_classification: This is a one-index correction. All asymptotic conclusions survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for some positive integers $p,q$ such that $p+q\leq 4n_0$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces a product of p factors by a product of 4n_0 >= p copies of (1+eps-c)/c, with c = 2 check f_min/(3 hat f_max). This is an upper bound only if (1+eps-c)/c >= 1, i.e. c <= (1+eps)/2. Since c can approach 2/3 (nearly constant symbol) while (1+eps)/2 < 2/3 for eps < 1/3, the factor can be below 1. In that case the inequality reverses (for p=0 the true product is 1). The stated C(eps) is then not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound each factor by max{1,(1+eps-c)/c} and set C(eps) = 2 max{1,(1+eps-c)/c}^{4n_0}.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant C(eps) in the superlinear bound may be invalid in part of the parameter range. The existence claim survives with a corrected constant.
issues.title: Invalid enlargement of the outlier product in the superlinear bound
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of constant preserves the theorem's form and rate.
